paper.title: Social Positions and Fairness Views on Inequality
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability statement (pp. 3115–3116): 'The data for this project are confidential. …

registers.name_in_paper: administrative records / register data at Statistics Denmark (tax returns)
registers.role: outcomes, treatment, controls, linkage, sample frame: individual income histories used to compute actual positions in all reference groups

registers.name_in_paper: Integrated Database for Labour Market Research, IDA
registers.role: treatment: identifies the start of disability insurance benefit receipt

registers.name_in_paper: Danish Sector Codes DB07 (sub-classification of NACE)
registers.role: controls / reference-group definition: sector of work
controls: vocational vs academic occupation; managerial position; promotion definition

registers.name_in_paper: hospital records (emergency room visits and hospital visits by referral from a general practitioner)
administrative records on workplace, address, house and car values, partner's income, parents' income and schools
registers.role: controls and reference-group construction: co-workers, neighbours, schoolmates, visible signals of income, family background

registers.name_in_paper: custom survey conducted with Statistics Denmark (not a register)
registers.role: outcomes and treatment: perceived positions, perceived P50 and P95, fairness views, importance of effort, randomized information treatment

linkages: Responses were linked by Statistics Denmark to the register data using the Social Security number assigned to all Danes at birth

respondents linked to all other individuals in each reference group (cohort, gender, municipality, educational level, sector of work, schoolmates, co-workers at the same workplace, neighbours in the same stairwell or on the same road) and to those individuals' register incomes
respondents linked to their parents' income positions when the respondent was 15 years old

sample.universe: Representative sample of 50,100 individuals born in Denmark in 1969–1973, randomly selected by Statistics Denmark and invited through Digital Post in February–March 2019
sample.unit_of_observation: survey respondent (individual); some auxiliary regressions stack respondent × reference-group observations
selection_rules: 50,100 invitations sent to a representative sample of Danish-born individuals from the 1969–1973 cohorts
13,686 clicked on the personal link in the invitation
drop respondents whose reported birth year or gender do not match the register data (19)
drop respondents who spent less than 10 minutes answering the survey (50)
drop respondents who did not report their income as instructed, e.g. reporting monthly instead of annual income (343)
drop respondents with zero or negative register income or missing background register data (61)
drop respondents who skipped one of the key questions (201)
9,415 respondents remain in the analysis sample
sample.period: survey fielded February–March 2019; register income histories reconstructed for the last 20 years; life events measured over a pre-shock period 2008–2011 and a shock period 2012–2017
sample.n_observations: 9,415 respondents (Table 1); 9,331 in the Table 4 regressions (8,854 for sector); 4,692 control-group respondents in Table 3 (4,452 for sector)

construction_notes: Income concept asked about in the survey and used from the register: wage income, self-employment income, and taxable income benefits and transfers earned in 2017; capital income, deductions and tax payments are excluded
Position in group: actual percentile position in the reference group's income distribution from 1 to 100, divided by 100 and centred at P50 in Table 3
Misperception: perceived minus actual position within the reference group, divided by 100

Unfairness of inequality: survey item on a 1 (completely fair) to 7 (completely unfair) scale, asked separately for each reference group with the group labels filled in from the respondent's own background answers
Importance of effort: survey item on a 1 (only luck) to 7 (only effort) scale

For small reference groups the perceived percentile rank is computed as X/N · 100, where N is the respondent's reported group size and X the reported position; the actual rank uses the true X and N from the register
Perceived P50 and P95 are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles within each group or bin in the figures
Local linear polynomials use bandwidth 20 in Figures 2, 5 and 12, bandwidth 10 in Figure 8, and bandwidth 100,000 DKK in Figure 7
Reference groups are the ones respondents believe they belong to (benchmark); Appendix Table A-3 compares these with the register classifications
Table 3 note states: 'A coefficient of 1 means that going from the bottom of the distribution to the top increases the outcome by one standard deviation'

Life events: pre-shock period 2008–2011, shock period 2012–2017; unemployment = three or more months of unemployment in at least one year of the shock period; disability = starting to receive disability insurance benefits; hospitalization = at least one emergency room visit or hospital visit by referral, excluding congenital disease, pregnancy and routine checks; promotion = switching from regular employee to a management position
